correctness.rationale: Exact enumeration of mappings by cyclic set, cyclic permutation, and rooted forest gives the cyclic-point mass function and tail law. Conditional component count is the uniform-permutation cycle count, yielding an independent Bernoulli-sum representation. A monotone coupling proves positive regression, while tail summation and Rayleigh moment convergence give the exact covariance formula and asymptotic constants.

evidence: Hansen--Jaworski 2006 develops exact distributions for cyclic points and components in a broad exchangeable-indegree mapping model and identifies the uniform mapping as a special case.
Hansen--Jaworski 2013 explicitly states that conditioned on m cyclic vertices, component count has the cycle-count law of a random permutation on m vertices.
Kupka 1990 gives the marginal distribution and moments of the number of components of a random function.

value.rationale: Cyclic vertices and components are foundational statistics of random functional digraphs. The theorem upgrades their relationship from separate/conditional distributions to a strong positive-regression principle for arbitrary increasing transforms and quantifies the mixed dependence on its natural asymptotic scales.
